note: Ps72 royal psalm (corrected; Book II close). Human IB = the ideal king's God-given moral rule: JUSTICE + RIGHTEOUSNESS, JUDGE the people, DEFEND (cause) the poor, GIVE-DELIVERANCE, CRUSH the oppressor, DELIVERS the needy, PITY the weak, SAVES, REDEEMS their life; the people FEAR God; the RIGHTEOUS flourish; closing doxology BLESSED be the LORD x2. God-qualifiers=4 (wondrous things, glorious name, God's glory). King's dominion/tribute/gold/renown + nature imagery (rain/grain/grass) + recipients (poor/needy/weak) = standalone. Every candidate roled.

dims.v: justice (mishpat - give the king your justice)
given by God, to rule with
paired with righteousness to the royal son

'Give the king your JUSTICE (mishpat), O God' — the prayer that the ruler be endowed with God's own justice; mishpat here the just governance the king must have from God to judge rightly - divine justice becoming the king's ruling character, the foundation of the ideal reign
righteousness (tsedaqah - your righteousness to the royal son)
paired with justice to the king

'and your RIGHTEOUSNESS (tsedaqah) to the royal son!' — the moral rectitude the king must receive from God; tsedaqah here the righteousness that makes the king judge the poor justly - God's righteousness given to be the ruler's own, the mark of the true king
judge / govern (din - may he judge your people with righteousness)
God's people, with righteousness; the poor, with justice
the exercise of the king's God-given justice

'May he JUDGE (din) your people with righteousness, and your poor with justice' — the king's governance in action; din here the ruling that puts God-given justice to work - especially for the poor, righteous judgment as the king's defining task
defend / judge for (shaphat - may he defend the cause of the poor)
paired with delivering the needy and crushing the oppressor

'May he DEFEND the cause (shaphat) of the poor of the people' — the king as champion of the powerless; shaphat here the vindicating of the poor's rights - justice that takes the side of the weak, the heart of the righteous reign
give deliverance / save (yasha - give deliverance to the children of the needy)
paired with defending the poor and crushing the oppressor

'give DELIVERANCE (yasha) to the children of the needy' — the king rescuing the helpless; yasha here the saving of the needy's children - deliverance extended to the most vulnerable, the king a savior to the poor
the reverse of defending the poor

'and CRUSH (dakah) the oppressor!' — the king breaking the power of the cruel; dakah here the shattering of the oppressor - justice that not only defends the weak but destroys their exploiters, the two sides of righteous rule
fear / revere (yare - may they fear you while the sun endures)
while the sun endures, throughout all generations
the reverence a righteous reign fosters

'May they FEAR (yare) you while the sun endures, and as long as the moon, throughout all generations' — the reverence of God the righteous reign secures; yare here the enduring fear of God among the people under a just king - good government drawing hearts to worship, faith lasting as sun and moon
righteous (tsaddiq - in his days may the righteous flourish)
the righteous whose flourishing marks the reign

'In his days may the RIGHTEOUS (tsaddiq) flourish, and peace abound' — the upright thriving under the just king; tsaddiq here the righteous whose flourishing (and abundant peace) is the fruit of good rule - righteousness rewarded when the throne is just
deliver (natsal - he delivers the needy who calls)
the needy who calls, the poor with no helper
answering the cry of the helpless
paired with pity and saving the weak (v13)

'For he DELIVERS (natsal) the needy when he calls, the poor and him who has no helper' — the king responsive to the cry of the destitute; natsal here the rescue extended to the one with no other help - the ideal king as the last resort of the helpless, mirroring God himself
pity / have compassion (chus - he has pity on the weak)

'He has PITY (chus) on the weak and the needy' — the tenderness of the just king; chus here the compassion that spares and cares for the weak - the inward mercy behind the king's saving acts, kingship marked by pity, not merely power
save (yasha - the lives of the needy he saves)
the act that flows from his pity
'and the lives of the needy he SAVES (yasha)' — the king's compassion made rescue; yasha here the saving of the needy's very lives - pity turned into deliverance, mercy that acts
redeem (gaal - from oppression and violence he redeems their life)
their life, from oppression and violence
their blood precious in his sight
the climax of the king's saving compassion

'From oppression and violence he REDEEMS (gaal) their life, and precious is their blood in his sight' — the king ransoming the oppressed, valuing their very lives; gaal here the redeeming (a kinsman's act) of the poor from cruelty - the king holding the blood of the lowly precious, the highest reach of royal mercy
bless (barak - Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel)
the LORD, God of Israel, who alone does wondrous things
paired with the blessing of his glorious name (v19)

'BLESSED (barak) be the LORD, the God of Israel, who alone does wondrous things' — the doxology that closes Book II; barak here the blessing of the God who alone works wonders (the qualifier) - the royal psalm rising from the king to the King of kings
bless (barak - Blessed be his glorious name forever)
forever, the whole earth filled with his glory
paired with blessing the LORD who does wonders (v18)

'BLESSED (barak) be his glorious name forever; may the whole earth be filled with his glory!' — the great Amen ending Book II; barak here the blessing of God's glorious name (the qualifier), with the longing that his glory fill the earth - worship reaching its widest horizon
wondrous things (pala - who alone does wondrous things)
God alone does wondrous things, blessed for it (v18)
v18 QUALIFIER (God's deeds): 'who alone does wondrous THINGS (pala)' - God's wonders are not a human IB char; the marvels for which he is blessed (282281). Qualifier.
God's glorious name, which is blessed (v19)
v19 QUALIFIER (God's glory): 'Blessed be his GLORIOUS (kavod) name forever' - God's glory is not a human IB char; the glory of the name that is blessed (282288). Qualifier.
God's name, which is blessed forever (v19)
v19 QUALIFIER (God's name): 'Blessed be his glorious NAME (shem) forever' - God's name is not a human IB char; the object of the closing blessing (282288). Qualifier.
glory (kavod - the whole earth be filled with his glory)
God's glory, which the earth is to be filled with (v19)

v19 QUALIFIER (God's glory): 'may the whole earth be filled with his GLORY (kavod)!' - God's glory is not a human IB char; the splendour the worshippers long to see fill the earth (282288). Qualifier.
righteousness (tsedeq - judge your people with righteousness)
v2: 'may he judge your people with RIGHTEOUSNESS (tsedeq)' - the righteousness manner of the king's judging (the char judge, 282298). Standalone (the righteousness of the rule).
poor / afflicted (ani - your poor with justice)
v2: 'and your POOR (ani) with justice' - the poor whom the king judges justly; the recipients of his justice. Standalone (recipients).
v2: 'your poor with JUSTICE (mishpat)' - the justice with which the king judges the poor; the manner of his rule (282298). Standalone (the justice of the rule).
prosperity / peace (shalom - the mountains bear prosperity)
v3: 'Let the mountains bear PROSPERITY (shalom) for the people' - the well-being of the realm under righteous rule; the flourishing of the land, an outward blessing. Standalone (societal well-being).
righteousness (tsedaqah - and the hills, in righteousness)
v3: 'and the hills, in RIGHTEOUSNESS (tsedaqah)' - the righteousness through which the land yields peace; the righteous order of the reign. Standalone (the righteousness of the rule).
poor / afflicted (ani - the poor of the people)
v4: 'may he defend the cause of the POOR (ani) of the people' - the poor the king vindicates (the char cause, 282314). Standalone (recipients).
needy (ebyon - the children of the needy)
v4: 'give deliverance to the children of the NEEDY (ebyon)' - the needy the king saves (the char give-deliverance, 282317). Standalone (recipients).
v4: 'and CRUSH the OPPRESSOR (ashaq)' - the exploiter the king breaks; the object of his crushing (282320). Standalone (the oppressor judged).

v7: 'may the righteous flourish, and PEACE (shalom) abound, till the moon be no more' - the peace/well-being of the realm; the flourishing condition of the righteous reign. Standalone (societal well-being).
bow down (kara - may desert tribes bow down before him)

v9: 'May desert tribes BOW DOWN (kara) before him, and his enemies lick the dust!' - the political homage/submission of the nations to the king; outward obeisance, not an inner operation. Standalone (homage).
bow down (shachah - may all kings bow down to him)
v11: 'May all kings BOW DOWN (shachah) to him' - the homage of all kings to the ideal king; political submission, not an inner operation. Standalone (homage).
v11: 'all nations SERVE (abad) him!' - the nations' service/subjection to the king; political allegiance, not an inner operation. Standalone (homage).
needy (ebyon - he delivers the needy who calls)
v12: 'he delivers the NEEDY (ebyon) when he calls' - the needy the king rescues (the char delivers, 306652). Standalone (recipients).
cry / call (shava - the needy who calls)
v12: 'the needy when he CALLS (shava)' - the cry of the destitute that the king answers; the appeal of the helpless. Standalone (the cry answered).
poor / afflicted (ani - the poor and him who has no helper)
v12: 'the POOR (ani) and him who has no helper' - the poor the king delivers (the char delivers, 306652). Standalone (recipients).
helper (azar - him who has no helper)
v12: 'him who has no HELPER (azar)' - the helplessness of the poor with no one to aid them; the king becomes their help (282652). Standalone (the absent helper).
weak / poor (dal - he has pity on the weak)
v13: 'He has pity on the WEAK (dal) and the needy' - the weak the king pities (the char pity, 282244). Standalone (recipients).
needy (ebyon - the weak and the needy)
v13: 'the weak and the NEEDY (ebyon)' - the needy the king pities and saves. Standalone (recipients).
lives / souls (nefesh - the lives of the needy he saves)
v13: 'the LIVES (nefesh) of the needy he saves' - the lives the king rescues (the char saves, 282248). Standalone (the lives saved).
needy (ebyon - the lives of the needy)
v13: 'the lives of the NEEDY (ebyon) he saves' - the needy whose lives the king saves. Standalone (recipients).
oppression / fraud (tok - from oppression he redeems their life)
v14: 'From OPPRESSION (tok) and violence he redeems their life' - the oppression the king redeems the poor from; the evil undone by his mercy (282255). Standalone (the evil redeemed-from).
v14: 'from oppression and VIOLENCE (chamas) he redeems their life' - the violence the king redeems the poor from; the cruelty his mercy undoes (282255). Standalone (the evil redeemed-from).
life / soul (nefesh - he redeems their life)
v14: 'he redeems their LIFE (nefesh)' - the life of the poor the king ransoms (the char redeems, 282255). Standalone (the life redeemed).
v15: 'Long may he LIVE (chayah); may gold of Sheba be given to him' - the wish for the king's long life; a blessing on the reign, not an inner operation. Standalone (blessing on the king).
pray (palal - may prayer be made for him continually)

v15: 'may prayer be MADE (palal) for him continually, and blessings invoked for him all the day' - the intercession offered for the king; the people's continual prayer for their ruler. Standalone (prayer for the king).
v15: 'and BLESSINGS (barak) invoked for him all the day' - the blessings called down on the king; the benediction on his reign. Standalone (blessing on the king).
name (shem - may his name endure forever)
v17: 'May his NAME (shem) endure forever' - the king's name/renown enduring; the perpetuity of his fame. Standalone (the king's renown).
v17: 'may his name endure FOREVER (olam)' - the perpetuity of the king's name; the everlasting extent of his renown. Standalone (temporal).
name / fame (shem - his fame continue as long as the sun)
v17: 'his FAME (shem) continue as long as the sun' - the enduring renown of the king; his lasting name. Standalone (the king's renown).
be blessed (barak - may people be blessed in him)
v17: 'May people be BLESSED (barak) in him' - the blessing the nations find in the king (the Abrahamic echo); the reign as a source of blessing. Standalone (the reign's blessing).
call blessed / happy (ashar - all nations call him blessed)
v17: 'all nations CALL HIM BLESSED (ashar)!' - the nations pronouncing the king happy/blessed; his renown among the peoples. Standalone (the king's renown).
forever (olam - Blessed be his glorious name forever)
v19: 'Blessed be his glorious name FOREVER (olam)' - the perpetuity of the blessing of God's name (the char, 282288). Standalone (temporal).
prayers (tefillah - the prayers of David are ended)
v20: 'The PRAYERS (tefillah) of David, the son of Jesse, are ended' - the editorial colophon closing Book II; a note on the collection, not an inner operation. Standalone (editorial colophon).
bear / lift up (nasa - the mountains bear prosperity)
v3: 'Let the mountains BEAR (nasa) prosperity for the people' - the land yielding well-being under righteous rule; part of the flourishing-imagery. Standalone (image).
rain (matar - may he be like rain that falls on the mown grass)
v6: 'May he be like RAIN (matar) that falls on the mown grass' - the simile for the king's refreshing, life-giving rule; the reign as gentle rain. Standalone (image).
v6: 'rain that FALLS (yarad) on the mown grass' - the descending rain of the simile; the king's refreshing rule. Standalone (image).
mown grass (gez - on the mown grass)
v6: 'rain that falls on the MOWN GRASS (gez)' - the shorn field revived by rain; part of the reign-as-rain simile. Standalone (image).
showers (rebibim - like showers that water the earth)
v6: 'like SHOWERS (rebibim) that water the earth' - the rain-showers of the simile; the king's rule as watering the land. Standalone (image).
flourish / sprout (parach - may the righteous flourish)
v7: 'may the righteous FLOURISH (parach)' - the thriving of the righteous under the reign; the flourishing carried in the righteous char (282331). Standalone (the flourishing).
have dominion (radah - may he have dominion from sea to sea)
v8: 'May he have DOMINION (radah) from sea to sea' - the king's universal rule; his outward reign over the earth, not an inner operation. Standalone (the king's dominion).
river (nahar - from the River to the ends of the earth)
v8: 'and from the RIVER (nahar) to the ends of the earth' - the Euphrates marking the extent of the king's dominion; a geographic bound. Standalone (the dominion's extent).
lick (lahak - his enemies lick the dust)
v9: 'and his enemies LICK (lahak) the dust!' - the abject defeat of the king's foes; the image of total submission. Standalone (image of defeat).
return / render (shub - the kings render tribute)
v10: 'May the kings of Tarshish and of the coastlands RENDER (shub) him tribute' - the nations bringing tribute to the king; political homage. Standalone (tribute).
v10: 'render him TRIBUTE (minchah)' - the offering brought to the king by the coastland kings; the homage of the nations. Standalone (tribute).
bring near (qarab - may the kings of Sheba and Seba bring gifts)
v10: 'may the kings of Sheba and Seba BRING (qarab) gifts' - the nations bringing gifts to the king; political homage. Standalone (tribute).
v10: 'bring GIFTS (eshkar)' - the presents offered to the king by Sheba and Seba; the tribute of the nations. Standalone (tribute).
precious / costly (yaqar - precious is their blood in his sight)

v14: 'and PRECIOUS (yaqar) is their blood in his sight' - the value the king sets on the poor's lives; the preciousness carried in the redeems char (282255). Standalone (the value set on their blood).
blood (dam - their blood in his sight)
v14: 'precious is their BLOOD (dam) in his sight' - the life-blood of the poor the king holds precious; the object of his valuing (282255). Standalone (the blood valued).
gold (zahab - may gold of Sheba be given to him)
v15: 'may GOLD (zahab) of Sheba be given to him' - the wealth brought to the king; the tribute/blessing of his reign. Standalone (the king's wealth).
abundance (pissah - may there be abundance of grain)
v16: 'May there be ABUNDANCE (pissah) of grain in the land' - the plenty of the realm under the reign; the land's fruitfulness. Standalone (image of plenty).
v16: 'abundance of GRAIN (bar) in the land, on the tops of the mountains' - the corn of the fruitful realm; part of the plenty-imagery. Standalone (image).
wave / shake (raash - may its fruit wave like Lebanon)
v16: 'may its fruit WAVE (raash) like Lebanon' - the crops waving like the cedars; the image of the land's abundance. Standalone (image).
fruit (peri - may its fruit wave like Lebanon)
v16: 'may its FRUIT (peri) wave like Lebanon' - the produce of the fruitful land; part of the plenty-imagery. Standalone (image).
blossom / flourish (tsuts - may men blossom in the cities)
v16: 'and may PEOPLE BLOSSOM (tsuts) in the cities like the grass of the field' - the people of the realm flourishing/multiplying; the reign's prosperity. Standalone (image of flourishing).
grass / herbage (eseb - like the grass of the field)
v16: 'like the GRASS (eseb) of the field' - the grass to which the flourishing people are compared; the image of teeming life. Standalone (image).
continue / propagate (nin - his fame continue as long as the sun)
v17: 'his fame CONTINUE (nin) as long as the sun' - the perpetuation of the king's name; the enduring of his renown (282273). Standalone (the enduring renown).
fill (male - may the whole earth be filled with his glory)

v19: 'may the whole earth be FILLED (male) with his glory!' - the filling of the earth with God's glory (the qualifier, 282295); the longed-for universal manifestation of God's glory. Standalone (the filling).
